title: Retroactive Tool Surface Equivalence Audit
summary: Record a retroactive FP-MCP-194-style equivalence and safety audit for the new tool surfaces added since FP-MCP-199: packet checkpoint recording, runtime diagnostics, execution gate orientation, and workspace change inspection. The audit distinguishes read-only surfaces from the non-executing packet-evidence recorder and checks whether any newly added surface structurally feeds execution authority.
caveats: This is a retroactive audit; the tools were already implemented before this explicit FP-MCP-194-style equivalence record was written.
The packet checkpoint tool is not read-only: it writes packet/evidence artifacts and commits expected files. Its equivalence class is non-executing packet/evidence recorder, not inspection.
The runtime diagnostics, execution gate orientation, and workspace change inspection tools are read-only/status/inspection surfaces.

The audit found a usability gap in gate orientation scope semantics: request artifacts are located by execution packet id, not approval packet id. That is a read-only orientation ambiguity, not an execution-authority path.
This checkpoint does not modify MCP bridge code; it records the audit result only.

auditBasis.rule: FP-MCP-194 standing rule for new tool surfaces: do not presume equivalence to a safer surface without explicit structural reasoning.
auditBasis.method: Trace each new tool's implementation module and server registration for request artifact creation/mutation, approval creation/mutation/consumption, disable-switch mutation, runner start endpoint contact, OpenCode start, FP-027/canary execution, network calls, writes, git mutation, and delegated dependencies.

toolSurfaces.reasoning: Although this tool writes and commits artifacts, its generated packet/result/verification text and returned boundary fields hard-code non-execution boundary observations. Its evidence script records packet/evidence/admission rows only. It does not import or call request-artifact creation, approval creation/consumption, disable-switch mutation, runner start, OpenCode start, or canary functions.

observedCommandPaths: optional opencode checks skipped unless configured
toolSurfaces.reasoning: The tool executes bounded binary availability/version checks and reads process/environment shape without dumping secrets. It returns boundary fields false for approval consumption, disable-switch clearance, runner-start contact, OpenCode start, and FP-027/canary. It contains no request/approval mutation path and no runner start dependency.

The tool composes read/status/validation/preflight-report functions and returns aggregate orientation. It does not call request-artifact creation, approval creation/consumption, disable-switch mutation, runner start, or OpenCode start. The live observed orientation also returned boundary.readOnly true and mutation/execution fields false.
toolSurfaces.observedScopeAmbiguity: If called with approval packet id instead of execution packet id, request artifact lookup can return REQUEST_ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND. Correct use requires execution packet id. This is a read-only orientation usability gap, not an execution path.

observedCommandPaths: optional bounded cat for safe untracked text excerpts
toolSurfaces.reasoning: The tool shells out only to read-only git inspection commands and optional bounded cat for non-secret untracked excerpts. It does not write files, stage, commit, contact network, consume approval, clear disable switch, start runner/OpenCode, or create execution artifacts.

auditConclusion.recommendedFollowUp: Defer fixing READ_ONLY_ORIENTATION_SCOPE_AMBIGUITY unless it becomes operationally confusing; continue to use execution packet id for request artifact lookup.
